newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Telecom Argentina seen heading for recovery.
newsitem.headline: Telecom Argentina seen heading for recovery.

text.p: Phone company Telecom Argentina posted yearly results below those of last year but mainly due to non recurrent charges and quarterly results may be pointing to a recovery, analysts say.
Telecom reported a $260.3 million net gain for the year vs $318.6 million, and a $55.8 million net for the fourth quarter against $72.0 million.
But yearly operating results rose to $491.0 million from $453.3 million, and in the last quarter they rose to $132.9 million from $113.3 million.

"The most important thing is that the fourth quarter was much better in revenues, most probably reflecting a better economy in Argentina and therefore more demand for phone services," Luiz Carvalho, analyst for Morgan Stanley said.

"Telecom is doing a very good job in terms of containing costs. It continued to reduce personnel expenditures and increase efficiency. That, combined with better revenues, have boosted operating profits in the last quarter and if the trend continues it will keep increasing them," Carvalho said.

Esteban Marx, head of research at Banco Comafi, agreed. "Yearly net was somewhat lower than expected due in part to higher corporate taxes, but operating results are good," he said, adding the firm had increased line digitalization to 95.6 percent from 85.6 percent a year ago.
Among the reasons for lower yearly net analysts mention higher charges for severance payments in a year the firm cut some 750 jobs, and they are upbeat about its outlook.

"In a tough year they improved productivity and invested strongly in its network," said Claudio Maulhardt, from Banco Republica. "And a low line density per capita in the country means there is room for the firm to keep growing."
Telecom is controlled by Nortel Inversora SA, formed by Italy's STET (32.5 percent), France Cable et Radio (32.5), Argentine conglomerate Perez Companc (25) and J.P. Morgan (10 percent).
